title: Several owned things: omitting meidän and teidän
focus: Omit meidän or teidän while retaining the ending; keep heidän in identification sentences.
targetSkills: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference
prerequisiteSkills: Plural possessed nouns in ownership sentences

exercises.prompt: Choose “These are their apples.” Keep the owner clear. Use omena (“apple”).
exercises.explanation: Retain heidän to identify the intended owner in this identification pattern; the shared third-person suffix alone does not identify that owner.
requiredSkills: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference
exercises.targetSkill: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference: form or meaning confused

parts.formation: Nämä is the plural of tämä: several things.

omenat (“apples”) loses its plural -t before -nsa: omena + -nsa = omenansa.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: demonstrative + agreeing olla + optional owner pronoun + possessed noun

parts.formation: Nämä is the plural of tämä: several things.
Use ovat with several things, independently of how many people own them.
Meidän is the personal owner form of me; it selects -mme.
talot (“houses”) loses its plural -t before -mme: talo + -mme = talomme.

answerDiagnostics.explanation: Drop the noun’s plural -t before -mme: use talomme.
Keep the possessive ending -mme even when the owner pronoun is present or omitted.
Meidän needs -mme; changing the ending changes the owner.
These are several things: Nämä needs ovat, regardless of the number of owners.

exercises.explanation: Nämä ovat identifies several things. The ending -nne identifies your ownership. Teidän can be omitted because the ending identifies the owner; the suffix stays.
